content.text: The
`AreaModelObjectArray`

class is a fundamental component of the GuiExpert Table library that 
represents a data model for a specific area of a table (header, body, or footer) where the data 
is stored as an array of objects.

This class extends
AbstractAreaModel
and implements
ObjectArrayHolderIf

, providing 
a robust implementation for handling tabular data where each row is represented as an object in an array.

The class provides functionality for:
- Managing row data (setting, filtering, sorting)
- Retrieving values from specific cells
- Handling row selection and focus
- Supporting custom sorting and filtering
- Accessing nested properties within objects
- Managing column order changes
- Applying custom CSS classes to rows
AbstractAreaModel
- The parent class that provides the base implementation
ObjectArrayHolderIf
- The interface that defines methods for accessing rows
AreaModelObjectArrayWithColumndefs
- A subclass that changes the constructor parameter order

content.text: The
`AreaModelObjectArrayWithColumndefs`
class extends
AreaModelObjectArray

to provide
a specialized implementation where column definitions are a primary constructor parameter.

This class is particularly useful when working with table models where column definitions
are essential for defining the structure of the table, especially in CRUD operations
and other scenarios where column definitions need to be explicitly provided.

The main distinction from its parent class is the constructor parameter order, which
prioritizes column definitions as a required parameter rather than an optional one.
AreaModelObjectArray
- The parent class that provides the core functionality
ColumnDefIf
- The interface that defines the structure of column definitions

instances. These instances will be triggered when the focus changes.

  (column groups), then along the rows (row groups, total row) – children in key order. This matters for

only: a row total adds its rows in source order, a column group merges its keys in key order, so
  the two may differ. Keys cut off by
still count in subtotals and totals.

Returns the index of the last fully visible row in the table's viewport.

This method retrieves the last row that is completely visible within the current
viewport of the table. A row is considered "fully visible" when its entire height
is visible without any portion being cut off by the viewport boundaries.

The distinction between "visible" and "fully visible" is important when scrolling:
- A row can be partially visible (some portion is in view)
- A row can be fully visible (the entire row is in view)

Repaints the table.

This method refreshes the visual representation of the table by delegating to the
tableScope's repaint functionality. Use this method whenever the table's visual state
needs to be updated after data changes, selection changes, or any modifications that
affect the rendered output.

Repainting the table ensures that all visible cells, rows, and styling reflect the
current state of the underlying data model and configuration settings.

Since 1.1.94 it also drops cached totals (
), so they are computed again from the changed rows. Scrolling never does that.

Performs a complete repaint of the table by triggering a hard repaint on the underlying table scope.

A hard repaint is more thorough than a regular repaint and performs the following operations:
- Recalculates the height and padding of the table model
- Resets the size of the wrapper div elements
- Adjusts containers and rows positioning
- Makes additional adjustments after scrolling

Use this method when regular repaint isn't sufficient, such as when:
- Table dimensions have significantly changed
- The structure of data has been modified (rows/columns added or removed)
- The table layout needs complete recalculation
- After major DOM changes affecting the table's container

content.text:
The AreaModelIf interface represents a model for a specific area of a table (header, body, or footer). It provides methods for accessing and manipulating data within that area. In the GuiExpert Table library, a table is divided into three main areas: - Header: Contains column titles and optional filter/sort controls - Body: Contains the main data of the table - Footer: Contains summary information or additional controls Each of these areas can be further divided into three sections: - West: Fixed columns on the left side - Center: Scrollable columns in the middle - East: Fixed columns on the right side 
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
 |  header/west   |  header/center    | header/east  |
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
 |  body/west     |  body/center      | body/east    |
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
 |  footer/west   |  footer/center    | footer/east  |
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
The AreaModelIf interface is a core component of the table's architecture. While simple tables might use basic data structures like arrays of arrays or arrays of objects, the GuiExpert Table library uses a more sophisticated model approach. An AreaModelIf implementation provides information about: - The number of rows in the area - The content of each cell - The styling of cells (CSS classes, custom styles) - Cell spanning (colspan, rowspan) - Row heights - Cell editability and selectability - Row selection state - Filtering and sorting capabilities This model-based approach provides maximum flexibility for creating complex, interactive tables.
TableModelIf
- The parent interface that contains area models
AreaModel
- A base implementation of this interface
AbstractAreaModel
- An abstract implementation with common functionality
AreaModelObjectArray
- An implementation for object array data

readme.text:
is the framework-free core of the GuiExpert Table: virtual scrolling in both directions,
millions of rows, zero runtime dependencies, MIT-licensed. The framework packages (Angular, React, Vue,
Svelte, Solid, Preact, Web Component) are thin wrappers around exactly this API.

**New here?** The [training](https://gui.expert/training/) explains everything step by step – 36 short
chapters with live demos. Every chapter links back to the classes on this site.

## Where to start

| You want to … | Look at | Training |
|---|---|---|
| create and control a table | [TableScope](classes/TableScope.html), [TableApi](classes/TableApi.html) | [First table](https://gui.expert/training/first-table/) |
| turn data into a model | [TableFactory](classes/TableFactory.html), [CreateTableModelPara](interfaces/CreateTableModelPara.html) | [Array<T> → model](https://gui.expert/training/array-to-table-model/) |
| define columns | [ColumnDef](classes/ColumnDef.html), [ColumnDefIf](interfaces/ColumnDefIf.html), [Size](classes/Size.html) | [ColumnDef](https://gui.expert/training/column-definitions/) |
| write an own header, body or footer | [AreaModel](classes/AreaModel.html), [AreaModelIf](interfaces/AreaModelIf.html) | [Own AreaModel](https://gui.expert/training/custom-area-model/), [Footer totals](https://gui.expert/training/footer-totals/) |
| configure behaviour and look | [TableOptions](classes/TableOptions.html), [TableOptionsIf](interfaces/TableOptionsIf.html) | [TableOptions](https://gui.expert/training/table-options/) |
| sort and filter | [TableApi.sortByColumn](classes/TableApi.html#sortByColumn), [TableOptionsIf.externalFilterFunction](interfaces/TableOptionsIf.html#externalFilterFunction) | [Sorting](https://gui.expert/training/sorting/), [Filtering](https://gui.expert/training/filtering/) |
| react to clicks, selection, edits | [EventAdapter](classes/EventAdapter.html), [EventListenerIf](interfaces/EventListenerIf.html), [GeMouseEvent](classes/GeMouseEvent.html) | [Events](https://gui.expert/training/events-and-context-menu/) |
| select and copy | [SelectionModel](classes/SelectionModel.html), [TableApi.copyToClipboard](classes/TableApi.html#copyToClipboard) | [Selection & copy](https://gui.expert/training/selection-and-copy/) |
| export to Excel | [TableApi.downloadExcel](classes/TableApi.html#downloadExcel), [ExcelService](classes/ExcelService.html) | [Excel export](https://gui.expert/training/excel-export/) |
| style cells | [CellRendererIf](interfaces/CellRendererIf.html), [GeCssColorUtil](classes/GeCssColorUtil.html) | [Renderers](https://gui.expert/training/cell-renderers/), [Heatmap](https://gui.expert/training/heatmap/) |
| show a tree | [TreeFactory](classes/TreeFactory.html), [TreeRow](classes/TreeRow.html) | [Tree table](https://gui.expert/training/tree-table/) |
| group flat rows with totals | [RowGroupFactory](classes/RowGroupFactory.html), [AreaModelRowGroups](classes/AreaModelRowGroups.html), [TableApi.setRowGroupBy](classes/TableApi.html#setRowGroupBy) | [Row grouping](https://gui.expert/training/row-grouping/) |
| pivot rows × columns with totals | [PivotFactory](classes/PivotFactory.html), [AreaModelPivot](classes/AreaModelPivot.html), [pivotRows](functions/pivotRows.html), [TableApi.setPivotConfig](classes/TableApi.html#setPivotConfig) | [Pivot tables](https://gui.expert/training/pivot-tables/) |
| update cells live | [TableApi.updateCells](classes/TableApi.html#updateCells), [TableCellUpdateEvent](classes/TableCellUpdateEvent.html) | [Live data](https://gui.expert/training/live-data/) |
| remember sorting and scroll position | [AutoRestoreOptions](classes/AutoRestoreOptions.html) | [Persist state](https://gui.expert/training/persist-state/) |
